title: Electrocyte stack: parallel-store, series-read capacitor quartet
idea: Electric eels get high voltage by firing thousands of thin electrocytes in series. Each cell stores its bit on four small sub-capacitors charged in parallel, and at read three in-cell switches restack them in series so the bitline sees about 4x the voltage. Each sub-capacitor needs only ~1.3 fF at AR ~20, instead of one 5 fF pillar at AR 70.
why: Capacitor charge wall (fact 1): trades voltage gain for charge, so the signal per fF is ~4x and the AR-70 etch goes away. The cost is extra in-cell devices, so it fits best in BEOL/3D tiers where area is cheap.

title: Chromatophore stretch-read: MEMS capacitor plate pulled away before sensing
idea: Cephalopod chromatophores change size because muscles stretch a pigment sac. Here the storage capacitor's top plate is a nanomembrane, and just before read an actuation electrode pulls it away from the node. With charge Q fixed, cutting C by 5x raises the node voltage 5x (V=Q/C), so a tiny low-AR capacitor gives a full-size sense signal.
why: Charge wall and AR (facts 1, 4): a ~1 fF near-planar cell could deliver the signal of a 5 fF pillar, with no AR 60-75 etch. A 50 nm membrane switches in ~10 ns.

title: Nacre brick-and-mortar perovskite nanosheet capacitor dielectric
idea: Copy nacre, where staggered aragonite bricks sit in a thin organic mortar. Tile exfoliated Ca2Nb3O10-type perovskite nanosheets (k ~200 at 2-3 nm) in staggered, overlapping layers bonded by a 0.3 nm Al2O3 mortar, deposited by flow-coating into the capacitor. The staggered seams force leakage paths to wander, the way shell deflects cracks.
why: Hits the k~70 target for the charge wall (fact 1): k_eff ~100-150 gives ~3x Cs per area, so AR can drop from ~70 to ~25. It also removes the Zr/Hf ALD dependence.

title: Butterfly-scale gyroid capacitor from block-copolymer self-assembly
idea: Green hairstreak butterfly scales grow a single-gyroid photonic network. Spin a double-gyroid block-copolymer film (~20 nm period) as a sacrificial template, ALD-fill one network with TiN, strip the polymer, coat with high-k, and fill the second network as the counter-electrode. The two interpenetrating continuous electrodes give a 3D capacitor with ~30-60x area per footprint in a 300 nm layer.
why: Charge wall and capital (facts 1, 4): spin-coat self-assembly replaces the AR-70 pillar etch and the support-mesh steps. Each cell is isolated by a shallow cut, not a deep etch.

title: Bamboo-node grow-up pillar capacitors with periodic diaphragms
idea: Bamboo reaches extreme slenderness by growing upward with a nodal diaphragm every few diameters. Grow the storage-node pillars bottom-up by area-selective TiN deposition through a sacrificial oxide stack, and add a thin SiN diaphragm lattice every ~150 nm of height. AR >150 pillars then neither lean nor stick, and nothing has to be etched at that AR.
why: Charge wall (fact 1): AR 115-150 gives Cs ~8-10 fF without a new high-k. It bypasses etch AR limits and pillar leaning, and uses cheap repeated deposition rather than EUV.

title: Mitochondrial cristae lamellar capacitor for lateral 3D DRAM cells
idea: Mitochondria pack membrane area into folded cristae joined to the body by narrow junctions. In a horizontal 3D DRAM tier, build the lateral capacitor from a thin Si/SiGe sub-superlattice inside the tier. Selectively etch out the SiGe to leave 4-6 thin shelves branching off a narrow neck, then coat them conformally as cristae-like folded electrodes.
why: 3D DRAM capacitor blocker (fact 2): ~3-4x lateral capacitor area per tier footprint, so the stack breaks even with far fewer than 26 tiers. Uses existing epi and selective etch.

title: Potassium-filter storage node sealed by a resonant tunneling gate
idea: K+ channels pass ions near diffusion speed yet block others because the filter is energy-matched. Put the storage node behind a double-barrier hBN/graphene/hBN resonant tunneling contact: during write the gate aligns the resonant level and current flows freely. During hold the gate detunes it by >0.3 eV, and transmission drops >10^6 because of energy mismatch rather than barrier thickness, so leakage depends weakly on geometric variation.
why: Leakage tail and refresh (fact 3): an energy-filtered off state could cut the <=13 fA tail 100-1000x and stretch refresh from 64 ms to seconds, saving most of the 16-33% idle refresh power.

title: Synaptic-vesicle quantal storage: Coulomb-staircase multilevel node
idea: Synapses release transmitter in fixed quanta. Make the storage node a sub-3 nm metal island (e.g. an Au cluster in SiO2) whose >100 meV charging energy quantizes stored charge into discrete electron-number plateaus. A single-electron-transistor sense node writes and reads four robust levels per cell, so the levels are set by physics rather than analog trimming.
why: Density and cost per bit: 2 bits per cell from built-in quantization, and the tiny node removes the capacitor. The main risk is room-temperature background charge noise.

title: Sodium-potassium pump ratchet: AC-powered in-cell self-refresh
idea: Neurons hold their resting potential against leaks with a local ion pump, not a central refresh. Couple every storage node to a shared global AC pump line through a tiny asymmetric MIM tunnel diode in series with a node-gated diode. Each clock cycle pumps a few electrons toward whichever rail the node is nearer, so 1s are topped up and 0s drained without opening any wordline or bitline.
why: Refresh (fact 3): removes refresh activations, recovering the 10-20% of bandwidth and most of the ~46 fJ/bit refresh energy. The pump current is pA per mat.

title: Persistent-sodium plateau node: sub-pA tunnel NDR keeps bit static
idea: Some neurons hold a bistable plateau voltage using a persistent sodium current with a negative-slope I-V. Add a vertical broken-gap interband tunnel diode (e.g. black phosphorus/SnSe2) from the storage node to a low rail. Its N-shaped I-V, with a ~pA valley current, creates two stable node voltages, so the cell latches statically like SRAM in a 1T1D footprint.
why: Removes refresh (fact 3) at near-DRAM density (~1.2x the 1T1C area, versus ~20x for SRAM). Standby power is the valley current only.

title: Cytochrome P450 spin-switch bit held at 85C mid-hysteresis
idea: Heme enzymes like P450 flip the iron spin state when a substrate binds. Fe(II)-triazole spin-crossover films have a 30-40 K wide thermal hysteresis that can be tuned to centre near the DRAM junction temperature (~85 C). Hold the die at mid-loop, write with a local 20 ns heat or field pulse, and read the 5-10% dielectric or resistance difference between the high-spin and low-spin states.
why: Removes the capacitor and refresh, because the state is bistable while the die is warm. The molecular film is solution-processed with no EUV, and die temperature becomes a resource instead of a leakage enemy.

title: Physarum oscillation-phase bit: nanomechanical parametron storing 0 or pi
idea: Slime mould encodes information in the phase of its cytoplasmic oscillations. Store each bit as the 0 or pi phase of a parametrically pumped ~1 GHz AlScN nanomechanical resonator: a 2f pump sustains either phase indefinitely, and a weak seed signal chooses which. Read by mixing with a reference phase on a shared line; many resonators share one pump line.
why: Replaces stored charge with phase, so there is no leakage tail, no refresh and no destructive read (facts 3, 8). AlScN is US-made and needs no EUV; energy scales with resonator Q (10^3-10^4).

title: Chlorophyll special-pair redox monolayer as the storage node
idea: Photosynthetic reaction centres store charge as molecular oxidation states. Coat the node electrode with a self-assembled porphyrin or chlorophyll-analog monolayer under a thin solid polymer electrolyte. Each molecule stores 1-2 electrons at discrete potentials, giving pseudocapacitance of ~50-100 uC/cm2, about 10x a high-k MIM, so a low-AR cell holds a full signal.
why: Charge wall (fact 1): ~10x charge per area could take AR from 70 to below 10 and remove the deep etch. Discrete redox potentials also allow multilevel cells.

title: Ball-and-chain nanomechanical plug isolating each storage node
idea: Voltage-gated K+ channels inactivate when a tethered 'ball' plugs the pore. Give each storage node a vertical nanocantilever contact that touches the bitline only while its wordline electrode pulls it in. When released, a vacuum gap gives essentially zero off-current, so leakage is set only by the capacitor dielectric.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3): off-current near zero lets refresh stretch from 64 ms toward minutes. Contact wear must reach >10^15 cycles, using hard Ru or carbon contacts.

title: Diatom silaffin chemistry: liquid-phase high-k grown inside deep pores
idea: Diatoms grow nanostructured silica at room temperature from dilute silicic acid using silaffin peptides and polyamines. Coat the capacitor holes with a polyamine monolayer that catalyses local hydrolysis of Ti/Zr/Nb alkoxides from solution. This builds a conformal 4-5 nm high-k layer that stops growing once it buries the catalyst, deep inside AR >100 pores and without vacuum ALD.
why: Capital and AR (facts 1, 4): conformal dielectric at AR >100, where ALD purge times explode, on liquid tools costing ~1/5 of an ALD cluster. It also opens Nb2O5/TiO2 (k 40-80).

title: Cell-membrane double layer: solid ionogel replaces the MIM dielectric
idea: Cell membranes work inside electrolyte double layers. Replace the ZrO2 stack with a 5-10 nm crosslinked ionic-liquid gel so charge sits in two Helmholtz layers at ~20-40 uF/cm2, 3-5x a high-k MIM. At ~10 mS/cm ionic conductivity across a 10 nm gap, the ionic RC time is ~ns, fast enough for DRAM writes.
why: Charge wall (fact 1): 3-5x Cs per area lets AR fall from 70 to ~15-20, and self-discharge over hours is far longer than 64 ms. The risks are thermal budget and faradaic side reactions.

title: Flytrap two-touch counter: analog leaky-integrator row-hammer sentinel
idea: The Venus flytrap counts touches with a decaying calcium signal and closes only after two touches within ~30 s. Give each row one extra storage capacitor that gets a fixed charge packet per activation and leaks through a calibrated transistor. When its voltage crosses a threshold, a comparator fires a targeted refresh of the neighbours, so per-row activation counting costs one cell's area instead of SRAM counters.
why: Row hammer (fact 9, flips at ~1k activations): per-row tracking at ~0.1% area, versus 1-3% for counter tables. The decay forgets benign accesses automatically.

title: Hemoglobin cooperativity: antiferroelectric window multiplies effective capacitance
idea: Hemoglobin releases most of its oxygen inside a narrow pressure window by cooperative switching. Bias the cell plate of an antiferroelectric ZrO2-rich capacitor so the 0 and 1 node voltages straddle its field-induced AFE-to-FE transition. The transition releases extra polarization charge, giving k_eff ~80-150 within the 1 V swing.
why: Charge wall (fact 1): reaches the k~70 target with no new elements, for 2-3x Cs at the same AR or half the AR. It does not store in ferroelectric hysteresis, so endurance stays near DRAM.

title: Mantis-shrimp Bouligand stacking breaks dielectric leakage percolation paths
idea: Mantis shrimp clubs resist cracks with helicoidal (Bouligand) layers, each rotated a few degrees from the last. Build the capacitor dielectric from 4-6 sub-1 nm crystalline sublayers separated by one-monolayer nucleation-reset films. Each sublayer then re-nucleates with randomised grain orientation, so grain boundaries never line up into straight through-paths.
why: Allows ~20-30% thinner EOT (higher Cs) at the same leakage, and trims the dielectric-defect part of the leakage tail. Uses existing ALD tools.

title: Lung-surfactant monolayer prevents high-AR pillar collapse during drying
idea: Lung surfactant lowers its surface tension as an alveolus shrinks, so small alveoli do not collapse. Before the final rinse-dry, coat storage-node pillars with a fluorinated phospholipid-like monolayer whose surface tension falls on compression. The capillary forces that pull AR >100 pillars together (stiction) then self-cancel as the gap narrows.
why: Charge wall via yield (facts 1, 4): makes AR 100-150 pillars survivable in wet processing without supercritical dryers or extra support meshes, for ~1.5-2x Cs.

title: Tree-resin wound sealing: self-clearing electrodes isolate leaky defects
idea: Trees seal wounds with resin, and metallized-film capacitors 'self-clear' by vaporizing the electrode around a fault. Use an ultrathin 2-3 nm TiN/Al top-electrode skin that oxidizes locally into an insulator when a leakage hotspot's current density spikes during a burn-in pulse. This disconnects only the defective spot and leaves the rest of the capacitor intact.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3): removes the dielectric-defect cells, so refresh is set by the bulk population, possibly a 2x longer interval, plus a yield gain.

title: Neuron first-spike latency: time-coded multilevel cell readout
idea: Neurons encode stimulus strength in their first-spike latency. Store four charge levels per cell and read by dumping the node onto a precharged line with a threshold inverter. A time-to-digital converter shared across 64 columns measures the trip time to ~10 ps, and that time sorts the levels instead of voltage-margin-limited multi-threshold sensing.
why: Density and cost per bit: 2 bits per cell (~1.8x bits per wafer), with per-row time calibration absorbing Cs variation. The storage element itself is unchanged.

title: Myelin sheath bitline: air-gap wrap raises cell-to-bitline transfer ratio
idea: Myelin wraps axons to cut their capacitance. Wrap each buried bitline in a sealed vacuum or air-gap sheath (k~1), segmented by short SiN 'nodes of Ranvier' for mechanical support, cutting bitline capacitance by ~40-50%.
why: Signal scales as Cs/(Cs+Cbl), so halving Cbl lets Cs fall ~40% at equal signal and the capacitor AR drop from ~70 to ~45 (fact 1). It also lowers bitline CV2 energy (fact 10).

title: Photosynthetic cascade trap: stepped wells carry electrons out of reach
idea: Reaction centres prevent charge recombination by hopping the electron down a chain of acceptors, each step further away. Build the storage node as a graded staircase of 3-4 oxide-semiconductor quantum wells (e.g. IGZO/Ga2O3/ZnMgO with stepped conduction-band offsets) beside a transistor channel. A write pulse cascades electrons into the far well, where back-tunneling is exponentially suppressed by distance, shifting Vt non-volatilely; an opposite low-field pulse reverses the cascade.
why: Non-volatile charge storage at low write field (~0.3 V steps instead of ~10 MV/cm Fowler-Nordheim tunneling), aiming at 10^9-10^12 endurance and ~50 ns writes. BEOL oxide process, no EUV.

title: Lowdin tautomer bit: proton-transfer hydrogen-bond ferroelectric layer
idea: DNA base pairs can flip protons across their hydrogen bonds (Lowdin tautomers). Use a proton-transfer organic ferroelectric, such as croconic acid or a designed base-pair-analog crystal, whose polarization flips when protons hop ~0.6 A along the H-bonds with no heavy-ion motion. It serves as a ferroelectric capacitor or FeFET gate layer.
why: Non-volatile, deposited from solution below 150 C, with no Hf/Zr. Light protons promise <10 ns switching and low fatigue; croconic acid shows ~20-30 uC/cm2 at room temperature.

title: Magnetosome biomineralization: protein-templated nanomagnet arrays without magnetic etch
idea: Magnetotactic bacteria grow uniform single-domain magnetite crystals using Mms6/MamC proteins. Anchor engineered Mms6 peptides in pre-patterned wells on a tungsten- and platinum-free spin-orbit write line (e.g. BiSb topological insulator), so each well grows one uniform 15-20 nm ferrite particle from aqueous solution. A tunnel-barrier read stack is capped on after growth.
why: Non-volatile. Removes ion-beam etching of MTJ stacks (MRAM's yield and capex bottleneck), narrows the switching distribution through uniform particle size, and runs as an aqueous room-temperature process.

title: CaMKII avalanche chain: small trigger magnet flips a stable cluster
idea: CaMKII holoenzyme subunits phosphorylate their neighbours, so one activated subunit switches the whole ring and keeps it switched. Make each bit a chain of 6-12 exchange-coupled nanomagnets. A short SOT pulse switches only the low-barrier 'trigger' magnet at the end, and the reversal runs down the chain as a domain wall; the chain's collective barrier (>60 kT) sets retention.
why: Decouples write current from retention: write energy is set by the small trigger (~5-10x lower), while retention scales with chain size. Non-volatile, with MRAM-like unlimited endurance.

title: Chiral-molecule spin filter writes magnets with voltage, not current
idea: DNA and other chiral molecules spin-polarize the electrons that move through them (chiral-induced spin selectivity). Put a monolayer of helical oligopeptides on a thin perpendicular magnet. A gate voltage charge-polarizes the molecules, briefly creating a spin-polarized interface that tips the magnetization, so writing uses only displacement current.
why: Non-volatile magnetic bit written at fJ level, with no heavy-metal SOT lines (no W/Pt) and no MTJ breakdown. The molecules are cheap and solution-deposited.

title: Venus flytrap snap-buckling nanobeam with coincidence-only write
idea: The flytrap leaf is a prestressed shell that snaps between two curvatures. Make each bit a pre-compressed buckled nanobeam (200 nm SiC or AlScN) resting up or down, read by capacitance to a sense electrode. Snap-through needs the row and column electrodes energized together, because either half-voltage alone only bends the beam elastically, which gives crosspoint selection with no transistor.
why: Non-volatile, with no access transistor, no leakage and no refresh. SiC beams at low strain have fatigue limits beyond 10^12 cycles, and MEMS fabs are US-based.

title: Statolith shuttle: nanoparticle moves between two ends of a sealed cavity
idea: Plant-root statoliths are dense starch grains that settle inside cells to record orientation. Seal a 10 nm conductive nanoparticle (Ru or a carbon onion) in a 30 nm vacuum nanocavity with an electrode at each end. An electrostatic pulse moves it to one end, where van der Waals adhesion holds it, and the bit is read by capacitance or tunnel current at that end.
why: Non-volatile with no bond breaking and so no material wear; ~1 ns transit over 20 nm and unlimited endurance in principle. Uses CMOS-compatible sealed air-gap processes.

title: Gecko peel-angle latch: adhesive nanoflap released by torque, not force
idea: Gecko setae grip by van der Waals force but release at once when peeled at ~30 degrees. Make the bit a hinged graphene or SiN nanoflap that sticks flat to either face of a V-shaped trench. A small electrode at the hinge applies peeling torque, so release needs ~10x less voltage than a straight pull-off, while adhesion holds the state with no power.
why: Non-volatile mechanical bit written at ~1 V instead of the 5-10 V of NEMS contact switches, which helps with the voltage floor (fact 10) and with stiction failure. Read by capacitance.

title: Hippocampal sleep consolidation: in-cell ferroelectric backup at power-fail
idea: The brain stores new memories quickly in the hippocampus and consolidates them into cortex during sleep. Coat each DRAM capacitor's inner electrode with 3-4 nm HZO and run it below the coercive field as a linear DRAM cap. On a power-fail interrupt, energy from a package hold-up capacitor drives all rows to write each cell's charge into polarization within ~10 ms, and the state is restored at power-up.
why: Data survive power loss while normal operation keeps DRAM speed and unlimited endurance. The ferroelectric switches only at power events, so ~10^5 lifetime cycles are enough.

title: Tardigrade glass lock: ions movable only during a heated write
idea: Tardigrades survive by vitrifying in trehalose glass, which freezes molecular motion. Store the bit as the position of Ag+ or Li+ ions in a 5 nm ion-conducting glass under a gain-transistor gate. A 10-20 ns microheater pulse lifts the glass above its glass transition so the field can move the ions, then quenching freezes them in place.
why: Breaks the speed-versus-retention lock of ionic memories by switching ion mobility thermally (~10^10 lower below Tg), aiming at decade retention at 85 C with non-destructive transistor read.

title: Mitochondrial nano-battery bit: emf read by a high-impedance gain transistor
idea: Mitochondria store energy as an electrochemical gradient, not as free charge. Put a 20 nm solid-state micro-battery (LixTiO2 | thin solid electrolyte | LixMnO2) on each gain-transistor gate. The bit is the electrode state of charge, which sets an open-circuit voltage ~0.3-0.5 V apart, read with no current drawn.
why: Non-volatile like a battery (months), yet read non-destructively in ns. Chemical potential replaces capacitance, so there is no capacitor wall, and writes below 1 V attack the voltage floor (fact 10).

title: S4 voltage-sensor gate: tethered ions flip between two sites
idea: Ion-channel S4 segments carry charged arginines that slide ~1 nm through the membrane field but never leave the protein. Make a gate dielectric with covalently tethered cationic groups (ammonium on short siloxane chains anchored to the oxide) that sit at one of two sites across a 1-2 nm layer. Their position shifts the transistor Vt, and the tether stops drift.
why: Non-volatile ionic bit whose endurance is not limited by ion loss or filament wear, because there are no free ions. Writes take ~10-100 ns at <2 V in a BEOL-compatible molecular layer.

title: Prion-templated martensite variants: compatible-lattice ferroelastic flip for endless cycling
idea: Prions convert their neighbours by templating their fold. Use a shape-memory-alloy film (TiNiCu-type) tuned so its martensite twin variants meet at geometrically compatible interfaces, the condition that let such films survive 10^7+ transformation cycles. A piezoelectric strain pulse switches a 20 nm cell between two variants, a remaining seed of the target variant templates fast growth, and the variants' anisotropic resistivity reads the bit.
why: Non-volatile, diffusionless switching (ns, low energy, with no melt as in PCM), with endurance limited only by lattice compatibility. No chalcogenides and no EUV.

title: Hydrophobic-gating nanopore: wet or vapor-locked pore stores the bit
idea: Many ion channels open and close as water fills or empties a hydrophobic constriction. Seal an array of hydrophobic 1-2 nm nanopores to an electrolyte reservoir. An electric field wets a pore (electrowetting), the wet state persists inside a hysteresis window, and a reverse pulse triggers vapor-lock dewetting; ionic conductance differs by >10^3.
why: Non-volatile bistability with no lattice damage, because the liquid simply refills each cycle; simulations show ns-to-us switching. Built from SiN or graphene membranes.

title: DNA supercoil topology: polar-vortex chirality as a protected bit
idea: Supercoiled DNA keeps its linking number until an enzyme cuts and passes a strand. In lead-free BaTiO3/SrTiO3 superlattice nanodots, store the bit as the clockwise or counter-clockwise chirality of a polar vortex, which is topologically protected against thermal flips. Asymmetric electrodes supply a curled field to switch it, and in dots where axial polarization is locked to chirality, the sign of the switched charge reads it.
why: Non-volatile at ~10 nm, where ordinary ferroelectric domains depolarize, so ferroelectric storage can scale below the ~20 nm FeRAM limit.

title: Entatic-state inversion: copper complexes whose geometry change locks electrons
idea: Blue copper proteins tune their geometry (the entatic state) to make electron transfer fast. Invert the trick: choose Cu(I)/Cu(II) complexes whose tetrahedral-to-square-planar change puts a ~1 eV reorganization barrier on spontaneous back-transfer, and place a dense monolayer between channel and gate. A gate pulse overcomes the Marcus barrier in ns, and the trapped charge shifts Vt non-volatilely.
why: Molecular-scale non-volatile charge storage whose retention comes from nuclear reorganization rather than thick tunnel oxides. Writes need low fields, endurance avoids oxide wear, and per-molecule storage could scale density.

title: Antifreeze-protein supercooled metal: liquid or solid nanodroplet bit
idea: Antifreeze proteins keep water liquid below freezing by blocking ice nucleation, and ice-nucleating proteins trigger it. Encapsulate a ~20 nm Sn-Bi alloy droplet in a nucleation-inhibiting oxide shell, so a melt pulse leaves it as a supercooled liquid that stays liquid at operating temperature. A second electrode with a seeding surface triggers crystallization on demand, and liquid and solid resistivity differ ~3-4x.
why: Non-volatile metallic phase change with no amorphous-chalcogenide drift, fast low-voltage metallic read, and abundant non-chokepoint metals.

title: Hin-invertase dipole rotor: molecular rotor crystal flips orientation
idea: Bacteria toggle genes when Hin invertase flips the orientation of a DNA segment, and the inversion persists through division. Use an amphidynamic crystal of dipolar molecular rotors (fluorinated phenylene rotors in rigid stators) with the rotation barrier engineered to ~1 eV. A gate field turns the dipoles 180 degrees in ns, and their collective dipole shifts an FeFET-like channel threshold.
why: Non-volatile ferroelectric-like bit from rotation inside a rigid framework, so there is no oxygen-vacancy fatigue or wake-up as in HZO. Deposited at low temperature from solution or vapor.

title: NiFe-hydrogenase proton loading: hydrogen-doped nickelate Mott switch
idea: Hydrogenase enzymes shuttle protons and electrons in and out of a Ni-Fe active site. Gate a thin SmNiO3 or NdNiO3 channel through a solid proton conductor: a write pulse injects hydrogen, which dopes electrons into the nickelate and drives it from metal to insulator (resistance change >10^3). The hydrogen stays put when unpowered and is pulled back out by reverse bias.
why: Non-volatile, multilevel-capable Mott switch read at low voltage, with large on/off ratio and rare-earth nickelates instead of chalcogenides. Proton moves of a few nm aim at ~100 ns writes.

title: Bone-marrow niche domain wall: conductive wall parked in pinning notch
idea: Long-lived plasma cells survive only in particular bone-marrow niches. Store the bit as whether a conductive ferroelectric domain wall sits in an engineered pinning 'niche', a notch in a thin-film LiNbO3 mesa between two read electrodes. A field pulse moves the wall in or out, and the wall's metallic conduction (10^3-10^6 on/off) is read non-destructively at low voltage.
why: Non-volatile, with non-destructive read, unlike FeRAM's destructive read (fact 8). ns switching, high endurance because no ions move, and US-producible LiNbO3.

title: Lotus-seed dormancy: ultra-wide-bandgap gain cell that holds charge for years
idea: Sacred lotus seeds stay viable for ~1,300 years by sealing a dormant embryo in an impermeable coat. Build a 2T gain cell whose access transistor has an ultra-wide-bandgap channel (Ga2O3 or AlGaN, Eg 4.8-6 eV) and a ferroelectric back gate that stays polarized to deep depletion when power drops. Storage-node leakage falls below ~10^-24 A, so a 1 fF node keeps its level for years.
why: Makes a DRAM-structure cell non-volatile with no exotic storage physics: DRAM-like write and read speed, unlimited endurance (charge on a node, no wear) and no refresh. BEOL-compatible.

title: Allosteric strain relay: piezo pulse precesses a magnetostrictive nanomagnet
idea: Allosteric enzymes switch an active site through a distant binding event transmitted mechanically. Put an elliptical magnetostrictive FeGa nanomagnet on a US-made, CMOS-compatible AlScN piezoelectric layer. A timed voltage pulse strains the magnet and rotates its easy axis, so the magnetization precesses 180 degrees in ~0.5 ns, and a tunnel junction reads the state.
why: Non-volatile magnetic bit written by voltage at ~1 fJ instead of ~100 fJ of STT current, with no SOT heavy metals (avoiding the tungsten chokepoint) and unlimited endurance.

title: Beetle-cuticle ferroelectric nematic: fluid polar bit that cannot fatigue
idea: Beetle cuticles and cell membranes are biological liquid crystals. Fill 20 nm cells with a ferroelectric nematic liquid crystal (RM734-class, polarization ~6 uC/cm2) between electrodes whose polar surface anchoring makes both polarization directions stable. A field reorients the fluid to write, and the switching current reads the bit, as in FeRAM.
why: Non-volatile, with intrinsically unlimited endurance because a fluid has no lattice defects to fatigue. Switches below 1 V at 20 nm and is filled from solution.
